column1: What is the core mathematical invariant of Vue's reactivity system?
column2: Given state S and expressions {f₁...fₙ} reading from S, a mutation to S must trigger re-execution of exactly the subset {fᵢ | fᵢ reads the mutated property}—selective invalidation with no stale renders.

column1: Why did Vue 3 replace Object.defineProperty with ES6 Proxy for reactivity?
column2: Object.defineProperty requires recursive walking of the object tree at init time, missing newly added properties (needed Vue.set) and array index mutations. Proxy intercepts at the object level (get/set/has/deleteProperty traps), providing universal coverage without recursive pre-processing.

column1: What are the time complexities of property access and update propagation in Vue 3's reactivity system?
column2: O(1) for property access/tracking, and O(d) for update cost, where d is the number of direct dependents of the mutated property.

column1: How does Vue's effect tracking system build its dependency graph?
column2: When a reactive property is accessed during a tracked context (render function, computed property), the access is recorded as a dependency edge in a directed acyclic graph (DAG); mutations traverse this graph to find and schedule dependent effects.

column1: What three problems does Vue's component model solve architecturally?
column2: 1) Encapsulation boundaries for template/state/logic preventing global mutation collisions. 2) Composable reusable units with independent instance state. 3) Progressive enhancement via deterministic lifecycle hooks.

column1: What are the three primary communication channels between Vue components?
column2: Props (parent-to-child, immutable, unidirectional data flow), Emits (child-to-parent event signaling), and provide/inject (dependency-injection-style data passing across ancestor/descendant levels).

column1: How does Vue's scheduler handle multiple synchronous state mutations within one event loop tick?
column2: It batches and deduplicates updates by queuing the component's update effect as a microtask, ensuring multiple synchronous mutations trigger only a single render pass.

column1: What are the two guiding invariants of Pinia store design?
column2: 1) Stores are reactive singletons—state participates fully in Vue's dependency tracking graph. 2) Stores are owned by the application, not the component tree—store lifetime is decoupled from component lifetime.

column1: What architectural failure modes motivate centralized state management (Pinia) over prop-drilling or event bubbling?
column2: Prop-drilling forces unrelated intermediate components to pass data they don't use; event bubbling through deep trees creates an invisible, undocumented API surface that breaks silently when hierarchy changes. Neither scales to application-level shared state.

column1: What JavaScript/browser primitives does Vue Router build upon to implement client-side routing?
column2: The History API's pushState/replaceState (mutate URL/history without network requests) and the popstate event (fires on back/forward navigation), wrapped in a reactive layer so components re-render on route changes.

column1: What is the first invariant of any routing system according to Vue Router's design, and how is it exposed?
column2: Navigation must be a first-class, interceptable operation. It is exposed through navigation guards—hooks that run synchronously or asynchronously during the navigation lifecycle to cancel, redirect, or augment navigation before the DOM changes.

column1: What is the second invariant introduced by SSR, and what happens if it's violated?
column2: The initial render must be deterministic and reproducible identically on Node.js (server) and the browser (client) from the same application state. If server and client state diverge even slightly, hydration fails silently/loudly, causing broken interactivity or a full re-render that negates SSR's performance benefits.
